root_cause.text: The macb GEM TX-ring recovery logic incorrectly reset `queue->tx_head` and `queue->tx_tail` to 0 on link re-enable instead of preserving/rotating the existing TX descriptors, which desynchronized the software ring state from hardware and could leave transmitted-but-unreaped SKBs stuck in the `macb_tx_poll()`/`macb_start_xmit()` path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the direct `queue->tx_head = 0; queue->tx_tail = 0;` resets from `macb_mac_link_up()` and replaces them with `gem_shuffle_tx_one_ring()`/`gem_shuffle_tx_rings()`, explicitly stating that resetting those indices “silently lost” queued packets, caused concurrent writes to `queue->tx_head`/`queue->tx_tail`, and made `macb_tx_poll()` wrongly think there were no packets because `queue->tx_head == queue->tx_tail`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the kernel gcd header so the file can use gcd-related helpers during compilation.
intent_record.what: A new include directive was added: `#include <linux/gcd.h>`.
intent_record.how: This makes the gcd helper definitions available to the translation unit at compile time, enabling code in this file to use kernel GCD routines or macros without unresolved symbol or missing-declaration issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add TX ring shuffling to realign descriptors and skb state so queued packets remain correctly tracked after ring wraparound.
intent_record.what: Added two new static helper functions: `gem_shuffle_tx_one_ring()` and `gem_shuffle_tx_rings()`. The first acquires `tx_ptr_lock`, reads `tx_head`, `tx_tail`, and ring size, computes the number of occupied entries, and if the tail is not at index 0, rotates the TX descriptor ring and associated `macb_tx_skb` array in place using a cycle-based shuffle. It also updates TX descriptor `TX_WRAP` bits as entries move, sets `tx_head` to the occupied count, resets `tx_tail` to 0, and issues a write memory barrier before unlocking. The second helper iterates over all queues in `bp->queues` and calls the one-ring shuffle for each queue.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this reorders each TX ring so that any queued transmit descriptors are normalized to start at index 0 while preserving their relative order and skb metadata. This makes the software ring indices match the hardware-visible layout after a wraparound or repositioning event, preventing inconsistent descriptor/ skb alignment and ensuring descriptor updates are visible to hardware after the rotation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop resetting transmit queue indices during MAC link-up so queue state is preserved correctly.
intent_record.what: Two assignments inside the per-queue loop in macb_mac_link_up() were removed: queue->tx_head = 0; and queue->tx_tail = 0; are no longer executed before writing the queue interrupt enable register.
intent_record.how: At runtime, bringing the MAC link up no longer resets each transmit queue's head and tail indices to zero at this point. The queue state is preserved across link-up handling, which avoids reinitializing TX bookkeeping during this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update MACB link-up handling to reshuffle TX rings after TX clock reconfiguration on non-EMAC hardware.
intent_record.what: The conditional block after `spin_unlock_irqrestore()` was changed from a single statement to a braced block. Inside the `if (!(bp->caps & MACB_CAPS_MACB_IS_EMAC))` path, the existing `macb_set_tx_clk(bp, speed);` call remains, and a new call to `gem_shuffle_tx_rings(bp);` was added immediately after it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, non-EMAC MACB/GEM devices will now not only reprogram the transmit clock when the link comes up, but also reshuffle TX rings. This changes link-up handling for those devices so TX ring state is adjusted along with the clock configuration, which can prevent transmit path issues after speed changes or link restoration.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a kernel gcd header for compilation support and does not affect macb TX-ring recovery, queue->tx_head/tx_tail handling, or descriptor synchronization.
The change directly addresses TX ring recovery/state desynchronization by shuffling descriptors and skb state instead of incorrectly resetting queue indices, which matches the root cause.
The change directly matches the root cause: it stops resetting the TX queue indices on link re-enable, preserving the software ring state instead of desynchronizing it from hardware.

The change to reshuffle TX rings on link-up directly targets TX-ring recovery/synchronization during re-enable, which matches the root cause of incorrectly resetting TX head/tail and leaving TX descriptors/SKBs out of sync.

candidates.rationale: This resets the software TX-ring head on link re-enable, which is the direct behavior described in the root cause and can desynchronize queued descriptors from hardware state.
This resets the TX-ring tail to zero during MAC link-up, losing the preserved ring position and leaving transmitted-but-unreaped SKBs stuck out of sync with the hardware ring.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line resets the software TX-ring head to zero during MAC link re-enable, which matches the root cause: the ring state is not preserved/rotated, causing software and hardware TX descriptor state to desynchronize.
This line resets the TX-ring tail to zero on link re-enable, discarding the preserved ring position and contributing to the TX-ring state mismatch that can strand unreaped SKBs.
